title: Priority claim: an edge-deletion matching-split identity for finite simple graphs and its instantiation on the prism graph - Lean 4 formalized proof + claim note (AI4Math pipeline)
description: Priority claim of record (not a full paper). Contents: the claim note (LaTeX source + PDF), the Lean 4 sources (Lean v4.34.0, mathlib4 v4.34.0 rev 5ed29652; 0 sorry; #print axioms whitelist-checked) and the audit and novelty-search evidence. Results: for any finite simple graph G with decidable adjacency and any edge ab, hosoya_deleteEdge_split_pts proves the edge-deletion matching-split identity mu(G) = mu(G - {ab}) + mu(G induced on the complement of {a,b}), the classical per-edge device of the matching polynomial / Hosoya-index literature, here stated for the matching COUNTING function the pipeline defines (mathlib has matching predicates but no counting API); and hosoya_prism_split_spoke instantiates it on the prism graph C_n x P_2 (delete one spoke, endpoints kept). Both compile with no sorry; #print axioms for both is exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Novelty adjudication, copied from the pipeline's C9 exclusivity review included here in full with every zero-hit query (three records: two review dossiers over six channels with 4 positive controls and the independent reviewer's confirmation): no occupying record found (reachable-channel scope) for the two defective-prism matching slices and the graph-side statement layer; value tier of the parent topic = new sequence (the mother sequence A102080 is occupied and not claimed); the graph-side bridge is graded first formalisation (Lean three-layer zero same-form). The identity itself is a classical human-maths tool and is claimed strictly at the tier first Lean formalisation (known unformalised), never as new mathematics; the packager ran supplementary arXiv sweeps on 2026-09-29 (all:"Hosoya index" AND all:prism = 0 entries; abs:"Hosoya index" AND abs:"deleted"/"edge deletion" = 0) and the mathlib v4.34.0 rg layer has no matching-count API.
